label: pre-training

candidate.notes: High run-to-run variance (41-57) driven by stochastic narration-instead-of-acting failures; the round-1 nudge catches most but not all.

reference.notes: Stable across runs; weaker at multi/hard tiers.

verdict: Pre-training, Pixie's default model and the reference tie at a median of 44/72 checks; the fine-tune must beat the median, not a single run.
method: npm run eval, identical 24-task suite, 3 runs: the post-fix validation run plus 2 same-day reruns (raw rows appended to training/eval-results.json, which was reset before the reruns and is gitignored).

label: post-training (Pixie-7B round 1)

candidate.model: pixie-7b (QLoRA on qwen2.5-coder-7b-instruct, 32 pairs, 6 epochs, final loss 1.189)
candidate.notes: Acts in ~1.4 tool rounds per task (2.3x faster than base) and never narrates-instead-of-acting. Wins all 3 head-to-head runs against the base model.

reference.notes: Base variance remains high across the day (its pre-training median was 44/72 with a best single run of 57).

verdict: Pixie-7B beats the pre-training median (53/72 vs 44/72), the reference model (44/72), and the base model in every same-run comparison (+20 checks on average). Fine-tune shipped into the CLI via /model → pixie-7b.
method: npm run eval, identical 24-task suite, 3 same-day runs per model after fixing a stale-GGUF incident: the first Ollama import had been built from the pre-fix (narration-trained) adapter; re-exporting from the fixed adapter (training/export-gguf.py) was required before scoring. Raw rows appended to training/eval-results.json (gitignored).

label: post-training (Pixie-7B round 2) — REGRESSION vs round 1

candidate.model: pixie-7b (QLoRA round 2: 105 pairs, 4 epochs, final loss 0.56, LR 2.5e-4, max_seq 1792)
candidate.notes: Still beats base in all 3 head-to-heads and still never narrates-instead-of-acting (avg 1.4 rounds/task). But the hard tier collapsed to 1/8 median (was 4/8): in run 3 it one-shots every hard task — single tool round, wrong or missing output — suggesting the larger dataset (longer command→save and two-edit chains, truncated system+tools prefix pushing attention toward training-time repetitions) made it more reflexive, not more capable.

reference.notes: Base had a particularly bad run 3 (25/72) and a good run 2 (39/72); same high variance as before.

verdict: Round 2 beats base head-to-head (3/3) but REGRESSED against round 1 (43/72 vs 53/72 median), driven entirely by the hard tier (1/8 vs 4/8). Round-1 adapter (32 pairs, 6 epochs) remains the shipped model until a round-3 recipe (fewer epochs on the merged dataset, or round-1 data + a small hard-tier slice) proves otherwise.
method: npm run eval, identical 24-task suite, 3 same-day runs per model. Fresh round-2 GGUF exported via training/export-gguf.py and re-imported into Ollama before scoring (export-gguf.py OUT path was fixed to always resolve to the project root after a cwd-dependent output bug put the first round-2 GGUF in training/pixie-7b-gguf_gguf/). Raw rows appended to training/eval-results.json (gitignored); logs: training/eval-post-r2.log, -r2b.log, -r2c.log.

label: post-training (Pixie-7B round 3) — REGRESSION vs round 1

candidate.model: pixie-7b (QLoRA round 3: 122 pairs, 2 epochs, final loss 0.933, LR 2.5e-4, max_seq 1792)
candidate.notes: Training was conservative and loss avoided round-2's suspicious 0.56, but the merged dataset still weakened multi-file behavior. The model continues to act on many hard tasks, but does not beat round 1 overall.

reference.notes: Base remains highly variable; round 3 beats it on checks in all three runs, but this is not sufficient for shipping.

verdict: Round 3 REGRESSED against round 1 (40/72 vs 53/72 median) despite the lower epoch count. Core held at 5/7, hard improved over round 2 to 3/8, but multi collapsed to 2/9. Keep round 1 as the target; do not ship round 3. Next experiment should reduce the dataset to a curated hard/multi slice or restore round-1 data balance rather than adding more traces.
method: npm run eval, identical 24-task suite, 3 same-day runs per model after exporting the round-3 adapter with training/export-gguf.py and recreating Ollama pixie-7b. Logs: training/eval-r3-run1.log, -run2.log, -run3.log. Raw rows appended to training/eval-results.json (gitignored).

label: post-training (Pixie-7B round 4, curated slice) — best since round 1, still short

candidate.model: pixie-7b (QLoRA round 4: 41 curated pairs — 38 verified hard/multi traces + 3 real sessions, 4 epochs, final loss 1.262)
candidate.notes: Wins all 3 head-to-heads. Core is now perfect (7/7 twice, 6/7 once — better than round 1's 6/7 median). Hard recovered to round-1-ish (3/8, with a 4/8 run). Multi remains the bottleneck (2-3/9 vs round 1's 4/9) — the curated slice traded away the simple create/edit variety that underpins multi-tier tasks.

reference.notes: Base stayed in its usual 25-39 band.

verdict: Round 4 is the best fine-tune since round 1 (45/72 median vs 43 round 2, 40 round 3) and beats base 3/3, but still REGRESSES vs round 1 (53/72) — do not ship. Core is solved; multi is the gap. Next recipe: round-1's original 32 pairs + the curated hard/multi slice (deduped) to restore multi-file variety without diluting the chain training.
method: npm run eval, identical 24-task suite, 3 same-day runs per model. Round-4 adapter trained on training/round4-curated.jsonl (rows 81-118 of all.jsonl = verified chain/two-edit/exact-N traces + real sessions), exported via export-gguf.py, re-imported as ollama pixie-7b. Logs: training/eval-r4-run1.log, -run2.log, -run3.log; raw rows in gitignored training/eval-results.json.

label: post-training (Pixie-7B round 5, r1+curated+multi5 union) — multi still capped, not shipped

candidate.model: pixie-7b (QLoRA round 5: 82 pairs — r1 recipe 32 + r4 curated 38 + verified multi5 12 — 3 epochs, final loss 0.839)
candidate.notes: Wins all 3 head-to-heads. Surprisingly, core DROPPED to 5/7 (r4 had 7/7) despite this union containing r1's simple creates. Multi only inched up (3-4/9 vs r4's 2-3/9) even though every chronically-failed multi shape now has verified training coverage. The added data did not convert into multi gains — and slight core erosion suggests the union still pulls the model away from round-1 behavior rather than adding to it.

reference.notes: Base in its usual band; round 5 beats it 3/3.

verdict: Round 5 ties round 4 (46 vs 45 median, both far from r1's 53) — adding verified multi5 coverage did NOT fix the multi tier. Two rounds of dataset-shape experiments (r4 curated, r5 union) have failed to move multi past ~4/9, while the retrained r1 control sits at 52-54/72 with multi 5-6/9. Conclusion: the multi gap is likely not a data-shape problem — suspect the training stack instead: r1 was trained at max_seq 1536 vs 1792 for r2-r5, and unsloth's fused-LoRA-kernel skip (lora_dropout 0.05) differs from whatever r1's original environment did. Next experiment: retrain the r5 dataset with EXACTLY the r1 recipe (max_seq 1536, 6 epochs, same LR) instead of the adapted recipe.
method: npm run eval, identical 24-task suite, 3 same-day runs per model. multi5 traces distilled with goal verification (9/12 first pass, 3 via multi5-retry.txt), dataset merged with the exported dedupe() helper, trained (18 steps, 1h48m, loss 0.839), exported via export-gguf.py, imported as ollama pixie-7b AND snapshotted as pixie-7b-r5 before scoring. Logs: training/eval-r5-run1.log, -run2.log, -run3.log; raw rows in gitignored training/eval-results.json.

label: post-training (Pixie-7B round 6, r5 data on exact r1 stack) — training-stack hypothesis REFUTED

candidate.model: pixie-7b (QLoRA round 6: same 82-pair r5 dataset, r1 stack — 6 epochs, max_seq 1536, final loss 0.123)
candidate.notes: WORST fine-tune round. 6 epochs overfit the 82-pair union into reflexes (loss 0.123 vs r1's 1.198) — the same collapse mode as round 2, now reproduced at max_seq 1536, eliminating seq-len as an explanation. Run 3 even LOST to base.

reference.notes: Round 6 still won head-to-heads 3/3, but by margins within noise.

verdict: Training-stack hypothesis REFUTED: epochs/seq-len do not explain the regression either. The full evidence now: r1 data (32 pairs, 6ep, 1536) = 52-54; r2 (105 pairs, 4ep, 1792) = 43; r3 (122 pairs, 2ep, 1792) = 40; r4 (41 curated, 4ep, 1792) = 45; r5 (82 union, 3ep, 1792) = 46; r6 (82 union, 6ep, 1536) = 36. The ONLY variable that correlates with score is adapter provenance — every retrained-from-scratch attempt lands 36-46, while both r1 runs (original + retrained from its exact data) score 52-54. Remaining suspects: (1) something in r1's original 32 pairs beyond their content — e.g. they were the ONLY data trained before the merge scripts changed message rendering; (2) stochastic seed interaction (SEED=42 is fixed, but r1-retrain matched, so unlikely); (3) unsloth version drift between the original r1 session and today's environment. Next step: treat r1-retrain (pixie-7b-r1, 52-54) as the permanent shipped model, restore the pixie-7b tag to it, and stop blind iteration — future rounds must start FROM the r1-retrain adapter (continue training) rather than from the base model.
method: npm run eval, identical 24-task suite, 3 same-day runs per model. Round-6 adapter = r5 dataset (82 pairs) trained with EPOCHS=6, MAX_SEQ_LEN=1536 (truncation check: longest pair ~1050 tokens), 36 steps in 22 min, loss 0.123; exported, imported, snapshotted as pixie-7b-r6 before scoring. Logs: training/eval-r6-run1.log, -run2.log, -run3.log; raw rows in gitignored training/eval-results.json.

label: post-training (Pixie-7B round 7, continuation from r1 adapter) — multi collapses, not shipped

candidate.model: pixie-7b (continuation round 7: resumed the recovered r1-retrain adapter and trained on 53 pairs — 41 curated hard/multi + 12 multi5, deduped — 2 epochs, LR 2.5e-5, train_loss 0.511, max_seq 1536)
candidate.notes: First continuation experiment (round-7 policy: stop from-scratch retrains). Adapter resumption verified live: continuation banner, 40.4M trainable lora params, and train.py's fresh-init guard passed. Core stays strong and hard matches round 1 (4/8 twice) — but multi collapses to 2/9 in ALL runs, worse than both round-1 variants (6/9 and 4/9). Even a gentle 10x-lower-LR continuation over verified chain traces erodes the multi-file behavior that round 1's original 32 pairs exhibit.

reference.notes: Base in its usual 29-39 band; round 7 beats it 3/3.

verdict: Continuation does NOT rescue the gap: 45/72 median — ties r4/r5, well short of r1's 52-54 — and multi is at 2/9. This refutes the last cheap recipe hypothesis: data shape (r4/r5), training stack (r6), and now adapter provenance via continuation (r7) all fail. Only the two runs trained on r1's original 32 pairs reach 52-54. Round 1 stays shipped; the multi gap points to something specific about r1's original data that none of the derived datasets reproduce — diff r1.jsonl against the derived pairs (rendered text + content mix) before any further training.
method: npm run eval, identical 24-task suite, 3 same-day runs per model. Round-7 recipe: the r1-retrain adapter was recovered by retraining r1.jsonl exactly (loss 1.197 vs 1.198 for the previous r1-retrain) and saved durably to training/pixie-7b-lora-r1redo (r6 adapter backed up first); train.py gained a BASE_ADAPTER continuation path (no second get_peft_model; frozen/fresh-init guards). Exported via export-gguf.py, imported as ollama pixie-7b, snapshot pixie-7b-r7 taken BEFORE scoring. Logs: training/eval-r7-run1..3.log; raw rows in gitignored training/eval-results.json.
